decided_not_asked.text: Only you start a stopped beat: your own fire (from the mouse, a key, a MIDI pad or another controller), play, or Resync. The autopilot does not, and a recording played in the review screen does not touch the live beat at all.

decided_not_asked.text: The picture in the review screen is made fresh from the recording each time, with the show it was recorded in; it is not a film of the night. So a curve you mend changes the picture you see; the show's clip files must still be on the disk (a missing one is marked as missing); and under a fast scrub a video clip's picture can lag a moment behind the mouse.
decided_not_asked.by: A recording stores moves, no video (facts-takes-bpm-fire.md section 1, VERIFIED); a film could not show a mended curve.

decided_not_asked.text: A recording will keep every slider and button of the clip, layer and global tabs from its first moment, mouse moves included. decided_not_asked.text: A recording keeps what every control did, whoever moved it: your hand, an action that was playing, or a signal. The row of a slider that a signal was driving shows what the slider did that night, with a mark that a signal drove it. So the review picture equals the night, as far as the recording's sound was kept.
decided_not_asked.by: His 169 words (a row for every control); facts-actions-open.md section 4 item 13. How the music's part is kept (stored values, or the recording's sound analysed again) is not measured yet: INFERRED.

decided_not_asked.text: Mending a curve never loses the night: the recording as it was made is kept, and you can go back to it.
decided_not_asked.by: His older rule never delete for stored audio (BD:520-521), applied to the recording; costly to undo otherwise.

decided_not_asked.text: A row shows its values in the same units as its slider shows them (percent, degrees, a number). You said radians for some; the app's rotation sliders count in degrees, so those rows show degrees.
